segments.he: אֵין שׁוּם עֵצָה וְתַקָּנָה לְהִנָּצֵל כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי
segments.en: That is, the above-mentioned concealment — that the light of the Tzaddik has become greatly hidden, to the point that he is very far from us on account of our many sins. And this is: "For he who consoles me has gone far from me, the restorer of my soul" — this is the true Tzaddik, who consoles and restores one's soul with the seven who restore taste [i.e., the seven types of leaders]. And on account of our sins he has been hidden from us and is very far from us — and therefore: "my children are bereft, for the enemy has prevailed". "My children" refers to the good deeds of each individual Jew, who are called "children" — for the essential offspring of the Tzaddikim is good deeds, as our Sages taught. And this: "my children are bereft" — because the light of the above Tzaddik has gone far from me, and therefore my children — even the little good that we still possess — are bereft and confused. For the enemy has grown mighty, that great enemy and foe, which is the evil inclination — in the aspect of the evil among the four elements — which is very difficult to overcome on account of the power of the above concealment. And upon all this: "I weep — my eye, my eye runs down with water" — as above. And through this very act of weeping in bitterness of soul and pouring one's heart like water, one merits — each according to one's level — that G-d will console him and draw down upon him splendor instead of ashes, until one merits to engage in Torah, which is the aspect of the waters of daas. And there the spirit of Moshiach hovers, in the manner of "and the spirit of G-d hovered over the face of the waters".

segments.he: כְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְהַתַּאֲוֹת וְכוּ' מִתְגַּבְּרִים עָלָיו מְאד מְאד. וְנִדְמֶה לוֹ שֶׁקָּשֶׁה לְשַׁבְּרָם. צָרִיךְ לֵידַע שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא עִמּוֹ. וּבְוַדַּאי אִם לא הָיָה לוֹ כּחַ לְשַׁבֵּר לא הָיָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגָרֶה בּוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע כָּזֶה. רַק אַדְּרַבָּא יֵדַע בְּנַפְשׁוֹ כְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע גָּדוֹל כָּזֶה.
segments.en: When one sees that the evil inclination and the desires and so on are overcoming him enormously — and it seems that it is difficult to break them — one must know that certainly G-d does not deal harshly with His creations. And certainly if one did not have the strength to break them, G-d would not have incited such an evil inclination against him. Rather, on the contrary — one should know in oneself: when one sees that one has such a great evil inclination, certainly one's soul is a very precious and holy soul in its root. For this reason the evil inclination overcomes him so — for the more precious and exalted the soul, the more the evil inclination overpowers it. As our Sages, of blessed memory, taught [Sukkah 52]: "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his evil inclination is greater than his." And as they further said: the evil inclination leaves all the nations alone and does not provoke except Israel — and moreover leaves all of Israel and provokes only Torah scholars. As it is written: "for he has greatly acted — for he stretched out his hand against the great ones" [Eichah 1:12] — precisely the great — and this is the aspect of King Dovid, peace be upon him, who was in great danger all his days. As it is written: "Pangs of death encompassed me, and the straits of the grave found me" [Tehillim 116:3], and: "I sank in deep mire and there was no foothold" [ibid. 69:3], and: "Rescue me from the mire so that I not sink" [ibid.] — and so throughout the entire book of Tehillim, which was founded upon the prayers that Dovid multiplied to be saved from the evil inclination and its armies, so that his soul would not be lost, Heaven forfend. And in this path every person must walk, for there is no counsel and no remedy to be saved from all this except through an abundance of prayers and supplications without measure, all the days of one's life — as King Dovid, peace be upon him, as above.

segments.he: שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי נַפְשׁוֹ הִיא נֶפֶשׁ יְקָרָה וּקְדוֹשָׁה מְאד מְאד בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ.
segments.en: And this is what the Tanna said [Berachos 17a]: "It is revealed and known before You that my will is to do Your will — and what prevents me? The sourdough in the dough" [i.e., the evil inclination]. For the sourdough in the dough is the opposite of the Supernal Will, and it is impossible to sweeten it and nullify it except through the shining of the forehead of Will [metzach haratzon], as above. And for this very reason our Master, Teacher, and Rebbe, of blessed memory, warned us very greatly to strive mightily to always have good desires and powerful longings for G-d. For the Will is the essential thing. As he explained in many places without number — and he spoke with us about this even more. For as long as a person, however he is, does not despair and strengthens himself with good will toward G-d and His Torah — through this he adds strength to the true Tzaddikim who are always engaged in drawing down the forehead of Will, through which they elevate from disfavor to favor. And this itself is the matter that the Tanna engaged with when speaking before G-d: "It is revealed and known that my will is to do Your will" — for through this very act of stating this before G-d, one draws upon oneself powerful desires for G-d, and through this very act one shines upon oneself the illumination of the above Will — to nullify the sourdough in the dough that prevents one from doing His will. And all this is the matter of the intimate conversation between a person and his Creator that our Master, Teacher, and Rebbe, of blessed memory, warned us about without measure. For the entire matter of this conversation is the aspect of the strengthening of the Will — through which the illumination of the above supernal redemption is drawn down upon him.

segments.he: וְעַל כֵּן מִתְגַּבְּרִים עָלָיו כָּל כָּךְ. כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁהַנֶּפֶשׁ יְקָרָה וְגָבוֹהַּ בְּיוֹתֵר. מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בְּיוֹתֵר. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה נ"ב) כָּל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵרוֹ יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עוֹד שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מַנִּיחַ כָּל הָעַכּוּ"ם וְאֵינוֹ מִתְגָּרֶה אֶלָּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְלא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינוֹ מִתְגָּרֶה אֶלָּא בְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים. כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כִּי הִגְדִּיל לַעֲשׂוֹת שֶׁפָּשַׁט יָדוֹ בַּגְּדוֹלִים דַּיְקָא שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה כָּל יָמָיו בְּסַכָּנָה גְּדוֹלָה כַּנַּ"ל. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים קט"ז) אֲפָפוּנִי חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת וּמְצָרֵי שְׁאוֹל מְצָאוּנִי וְכוּ'. (שָׁם סט) טָבַעְתִּי בִּיוֵן מְצוּלָה וְאֵין מָעֳמָד וְכוּ'. הַצִּילֵנִי מִטִּיט וְאַל אֶטְבָּעָה וְכוּ'. וְכֵן כָּל סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים שֶׁנִּתְיַסֵּד מֵהַתְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁהִרְבָּה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְהִנָּצֵל מֵהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְחֵילוֹתָיו לְבַל יאבַד נַפְשׁוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. וּבְדֶרֶךְ זֶה צָרִיךְ כָּל אָדָם לֵילֵךְ כִּי אֵין שׁוּם עֵצָה וְתַקָּנָה לְהִנָּצֵל מִכָּל זֶה כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי תְּפִלּוֹת וְתַחֲנוּנִים בְּלִי שִׁעוּר כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו כְּמוֹ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כַּנַּ"ל וְכַמְבאָר אֶצְלֵנוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים. (הִלְכוֹת בִּרְכַּת הַשַּׁחַר הֲלָכָה ג אוֹת ד):
segments.en: And one must be very strong in this without measure and estimation — and then ultimately one will certainly merit that everything will be sweetened through the power of the Tzaddik who is engaged in the comprehensive redemption. And then everything will be transformed for the good, for there everything is rectified.
